bugs.title: the engine crashed when a function outlived the block it was defined in
bugs.summary: Functions created inside a certain kind of block kept pointing at scratch space the engine had already thrown away. Calling one of those functions later crashed the program, and nothing hinted at the real cause.
bugs.why_critical: It was a memory safety fault that only showed up long after the damage was done, so it was very hard to trace.
bugs.evidence_quote: WITH_END was freeing the with-env EnvRecord via libc::free on scope exit. Closures created inside the `with` block captured act.var_env (pointing to this env record) via the CLOSURE opcode, leaving a dangling pointer.
bugs.latency_signal: Silent until closure invoked; discovered through with-statement test suite
bugs.credit: found and fixed by deepseek-v4-flash in Crush
bugs.line: engine crashed when a function outlived its block
bugs.label: 24 May

bugs.title: repeated pattern matching hung forever instead of finishing
bugs.summary: Searching text for all matches always restarted from the beginning, so loops that walked through every match never ran out of work. The program just hung, with no error.
bugs.why_critical: A very common way of scanning text never terminated.
bugs.evidence_quote: Previously, exec/test always started matching from position 0, ignoring lastIndex. This caused infinite loops in do...while patterns that iterate over global matches (6 hanging RegExp tests now pass).
bugs.latency_signal: Silent infinite loop; discovered via test262 suite hanging on 6 RegExp tests
bugs.credit: found and fixed by deepseek-v4-flash in Crush
bugs.line: repeated pattern matching hung forever instead of finishing
bugs.label: 24 May

bugs.title: skipping an iteration in a for-of loop hung the program
bugs.summary: Asking a for-of loop to jump to the next item sent it back to the start of the same item instead, so it never moved on. The program hung with no error.
bugs.why_critical: A common combination of two ordinary language features silently froze, and the tests never covered it.
bugs.evidence_quote: continue_target was set to the LT comparison, causing continue to re-enter the same iteration without advancing the index.
bugs.latency_signal: Silent infinite loop; discovered by examining for-of edge case handling
bugs.credit: found and fixed by deepseek-v4-pro in Crush
bugs.line: skipping an iteration in a for-of loop hung the program
bugs.label: 25 May

bugs.title: the test runner ballooned past 90GB of memory and died
bugs.summary: Shutting down never actually released the text and compiled code a test had created, so every test added to a pile that was never cleared. Memory grew without limit until the machine ran out.
bugs.why_critical: Nothing ever raised an error, so it was only noticed once the test suite hit the ceiling.
bugs.evidence_quote: Heap.destroy was not freeing individual HString objects in the open-addressed string table (only the bucket array), and CompiledFunction objects allocated by the compiler were never tracked or freed. Each batch_test_vm test created a fresh heap that leaked all its strings and compiled functions, causing unbounded memory growth.
bugs.latency_signal: Silent unbounded growth discovered when test suite hit 90GB+ limit
bugs.credit: found and fixed by mimo-v2.5 in Crush
bugs.line: test runner ballooned past 90GB of memory and died
bugs.label: 27 May

bugs.title: zero and the empty string counted as true, so loops never ended
bugs.summary: The check for whether a value counts as true only recognised a few cases, so the number zero and an empty piece of text both looked true. Loops written to stop on those conditions ran forever.
bugs.why_critical: It broke one of the most basic rules of the language with no clue as to why.
bugs.evidence_quote: The NaNBox is_truthy macro only handled UNDEFINED, NULL, and BOOLEAN (false) as falsy. FASTINT 0 and empty STRING fell through to return true, causing infinite loops in while(0), while(\"\"), do-while(0), etc.
bugs.latency_signal: Silent infinite loops discovered through test execution
bugs.credit: found and fixed by mimo-v2.5 in Crush
bugs.line: zero and the empty string counted as true
bugs.label: 29 May

bugs.title: assigning to an object using square brackets did nothing
bugs.summary: The compiler turned a write into a read, so setting a value by computed key was silently discarded. No error, the value simply never changed.
bugs.why_critical: A fundamental part of the language quietly did not work.
bugs.evidence_quote: The inner expression() call inside the bracket handler of member_expr() calls assignment_expr(), which resets lhs_mode to false. This clobbered the outer lhs_mode=true state needed for PUTPROP emission.
bugs.latency_signal: Silent loss of assignment effect; discovered through test262 jump by 1033 passes
bugs.credit: found and fixed by mimo-v2.5-pro in Crush
bugs.line: assigning to an object using square brackets did nothing
bugs.label: 29 May

bugs.title: every comparison could silently return the wrong answer
bugs.summary: When a comparison stored its answer in the same slot it was about to read from, it destroyed the number first and then compared against garbage, always answering false. That broke every for-loop in the language.
bugs.why_critical: No error appeared, just wrong results, so basic control flow was quietly broken.
bugs.evidence_quote: When ra aliases rb (e.g. LE r1 = r1, r2), set_boolean(false) clobbered the source operand before the comparison, always yielding false. This broke all for-loops and any comparison where the result register matched an input register.
bugs.latency_signal: Silent wrong values; discovered through for-loop test suite never executing
bugs.credit: found and fixed by an unidentified agent (Pi)
bugs.line: every comparison could silently return the wrong answer
bugs.label: 1 Jun

bugs.title: returning from a function corrupted memory and crashed at random
bugs.summary: The path that returned from a function left the engine's bookkeeping in a bad state, so the memory cleaner threw away things that were still in use. The same program would crash unpredictably from one run to the next.
bugs.why_critical: Random crashes on identical input are among the hardest failures to chase down.
bugs.evidence_quote: GC could collect objects whose pointers were still cached in IC entries because valstack_top wasn't properly restored for the caller, causing mark_activations to miss live registers.
bugs.latency_signal: Non-deterministic Unknown opcode crashes in bench_property_lookup; heap-state dependent
bugs.credit: found and fixed by mimo-v2.5-pro in Crush
bugs.line: returning from a function corrupted memory at random
bugs.label: 2 Jun

bugs.title: the memory cleaner read half-built function calls and corrupted the heap
bugs.summary: A function call was announced as live before its details had been filled in, so if cleanup ran at that instant it followed leftover junk from an older call. That quietly damaged memory while new objects were being created.
bugs.why_critical: Corrupting the heap during allocation can break anything, anywhere, later on.
bugs.evidence_quote: Incremented activation_count before env_create_function_scope, making activation visible to vm_mark_activations while var_env/lex_env held stale pointers from reused slot. This caused GC to follow garbage EnvRecord->bindings pointers.
bugs.latency_signal: Deterministic VM_ERROR on bench_valstack_copy; found in deep recursion patterns
bugs.credit: found and fixed by deepseek-v4-pro in Crush
bugs.line: memory cleaner corrupted the heap mid-call
bugs.label: 8 Jun

bugs.title: assigning to an object property quietly overwrote nearby variables
bugs.summary: Whenever a property assignment invoked user code, it scribbled over up to four of the calling function's own local variables. Any program using property accessors got silently wrong values.
bugs.why_critical: It corrupted variables engine wide with no error, so it sat as a time bomb until accessors were used.
bugs.evidence_quote: PUTPROP's A/B/C are arbitrary live locals, so invoking any JS setter from inside a function silently corrupted caller variables (test262 propertyHelper verifyWritable broke on every accessor property).
bugs.latency_signal: Silent wrong values discovered when test262 uses accessor properties in descriptor tests
bugs.credit: found and fixed by claude-fable-5 in Claude Code
bugs.line: setting a property quietly overwrote nearby variables
bugs.label: 13 Jun

bugs.title: automatic memory cleanup crashed while objects were still being built
bugs.summary: Cleanup could kick in in the middle of allocating something, freeing an object that had been created but not yet handed to anyone. The result was unpredictable crashes from freeing the same memory twice.
bugs.why_critical: It broke a core assumption that cleanup never runs partway through building an object.
bugs.evidence_quote: Periodic GC in Heap.alloc/realloc was running mark-and-sweep inline, which could free objects still held only in C3 locals (refcount 0, not yet anchored). This caused nondeterministic double-free crashes in FixedBlockPool.
bugs.latency_signal: Nondeterministic flaky crashes found by workers dying in defineProperty tests
bugs.credit: found and fixed by mimo-v2.5-pro in Crush
bugs.line: memory cleanup crashed while objects were half-built
bugs.label: 13 Jun

bugs.title: resetting the engine left it pointing at memory it had just released
bugs.summary: A handful of cached values survived a reset even though the memory behind them was gone. Anything that touched them afterwards worked on freed memory.
bugs.why_critical: It left a hidden landmine that would corrupt later operations without warning.
bugs.evidence_quote: Heap.reset: clear error_value, yield_value, lj.value1/value2 TVal fields and iterator_symbol/toprimitive_symbol HString* caches that survive reset and point into freed pool/string-table memory.
bugs.latency_signal: UAF when stale caches dereferenced; manifested in subsequent operations after reset
bugs.credit: found and fixed by deepseek-v4-pro in Crush
bugs.line: resetting the engine left it using freed memory
bugs.label: 14 Jun

bugs.title: every uncaught error printed a crash dump instead of the real message
bugs.summary: When an error had nowhere to go, the engine threw away the message and died with an internal crash dump. A simple typo that should have said "x is not defined" looked like the engine itself had broken.
bugs.why_critical: Error reporting was useless across the whole engine, and the same path was unsafe with memory too.
bugs.evidence_quote: all uncaught exceptions (x = 1; print(x); → 'ReferenceError: x is not defined' was thrown but never surfaced); the 50+ opcode handlers...just returned VM_ERROR~ directly, dropping the thrown value
bugs.latency_signal: Systemic uncaught-exception bug discovered through crash dump analysis; every uncaught exception crashed
bugs.credit: found and fixed by minimax-m3 in opencode
bugs.line: every uncaught error printed a crash dump
bugs.label: 21 Jun

bugs.title: pre-filled function arguments were thrown away while still in use
bugs.summary: Functions with arguments locked in ahead of time released those values too early. The freed space got handed to the next such function, which then wrote over the original object.
bugs.why_critical: It silently corrupted data for any code using that common pattern with object arguments.
bugs.evidence_quote: The result was a net over-decref: a heap value passed as a bound argument (e.g. a TypedArray constructor via `factory.bind(undefined, Float64Array)`) was freed while still live. Its pool block was then recycled into the next bound function, whose `.name = "bound <target>"` write corrupted the original object
bugs.latency_signal: 91.2% -> 92.1% (+258 pass); affected all testWithTypedArrayConstructors patterns
bugs.credit: found and fixed by claude-opus-4.8 in Claude Code
bugs.line: pre-filled function arguments were thrown away
bugs.label: 10 Jul

bugs.title: two identical strings could compare as different
bugs.summary: A shortcut in string joining produced text the engine did not register in its shared table, and the engine compares text by identity rather than contents. Searching for a string you had just built returned "not found" even though a direct equality check said it was there.
bugs.why_critical: It produced wrong answers in ordinary code with no error at all, and only appeared after a speed optimization was switched on.
bugs.evidence_quote: The skip-intern accumulator fast path (ra aliases a source register) produced un-interned HStrings... String equality across the engine... is pointer identity on the interned HString, so an un-interned concat result that escapes... compares unequal to the interned literal with the same contents: cat4.indexOf('(())') returned -1 while cat4[0] === '(())' was true.
bugs.latency_signal: Silent until moveelim optimization activated aliased ADD emission
bugs.credit: found and fixed by claude-fable-5 in Claude Code
bugs.line: two identical strings could compare as different
bugs.label: 23 Jul

bugs.title: two broken cases in building an array from async data had been passing by accident
bugs.summary: An unrelated defect was swallowing the failures, so these tests looked green. Once it was fixed, symbols went down the wrong path and certain errors returned nothing instead of a rejected result.
bugs.why_critical: One bug was hiding another, so the test suite gave false confidence.
bugs.evidence_quote: Both were false-passes before ef32064: the stale-channel leak it fixed was silently swallowing these tests' rejections. A Symbol primitive wrapped for the array-like path got string_proto... so fromAsync found String.prototype[@@iterator] and rejected... instead of using Symbol.prototype array-like reads.
bugs.latency_signal: Masked by channel leak; bug-hiding bug
bugs.credit: found and fixed by claude-fable-5 in Claude Code
bugs.line: two broken cases in building an array from async data had been passing by ac
bugs.label: 23 Jul

bugs.title: long strings piled up in memory and were sometimes freed too early
bugs.summary: Large pieces of text had no safety net, so several common operations either lost track of them forever or released them while still in use. A single measured workload left roughly 2000 stray objects behind.
bugs.why_critical: Several separate leaks sat in the busiest code paths and grew without any limit.
bugs.evidence_quote: Large non-interned strings... are pure refcounted leaves with no string-table or mark-sweep backstop: any register write that clobbers the last owned reference leaks the block permanently. Measured with `leaks --atExit`: call-result string 2015→15, discarded-result 2015→15, concat-into-number 2015→15, return-from-try Catcher 5015→15
bugs.latency_signal: Measured via leaks/ASan; ~2000 leaked objects per workload
bugs.credit: found and fixed by claude-fable-5 in Claude Code
bugs.line: long strings piled up in memory and were sometimes freed too early
bugs.label: 24 Jul

bugs.title: classes with more than 64 private fields aliased or crashed
bugs.summary: Parts of the compiler kept their own stale copies of a shared list of private field names. As soon as that list grew past its initial size of 64, the leftovers pointed at released memory and names collided or the compiler crashed.
bugs.why_critical: It only bit at the 65th private name, so it hid easily while quietly reading freed memory.
bugs.evidence_quote: each CompilerContext held its own copy of the (entries, count, cap) triple. When a borrowing context... declared private names via a nested class in a field initializer, it grew its OWN copy and reallocated the shared entries buffer — leaving the owner and every sibling borrower with a stale pointer into freed memory. The 65th private name (first realloc past the initial cap of 64) therefore aliased or crashed
bugs.latency_signal: Silent until >64 private fields in nested contexts
bugs.credit: found and fixed by claude-fable-5 in Claude Code
bugs.line: classes with more than 64 private fields aliased or crashed
bugs.label: 24 Jul

bugs.title: every paused async function leaked, and cleanup crashed the engine
bugs.summary: The state kept for a suspended async function was never released, so all of them leaked, and a full cleanup pass segfaulted outright. It had been there all along without any test noticing.
bugs.why_critical: It combined permanent leaks with an outright crash during memory cleanup.
bugs.evidence_quote: hobject_free never freed this GS at all, leaking the struct (and its saved_regs/this_binding) on every async function that suspends at least once... the baseline binary (4fe6cfe9) segfaults outright on the same completed-2000 repro once a full mark-and-sweep pass runs, from the reaction-chain `.next` bug
bugs.latency_signal: Pre-existing bug; only surfaced when GeneratorState was finally freed and GC pressure exposed untracked reaction chains
bugs.credit: found and fixed by claude-opus-5 in Claude Code
bugs.line: every paused async function leaked
bugs.label: 29 Jul

bugs.title: listing the keys of a proxy object could segfault
bugs.summary: The list of keys was freed partway through being read, because nothing told the memory cleaner it was still in use. A proxy with 50 or more keys crashed the process under memory pressure.
bugs.why_critical: It read freed memory during a common loop and killed the process outright.
bugs.evidence_quote: The array was reachable only from a C3 local the mark phase cannot see, so it was collected partway through the loop and the next arr.array_part()[i] read freed memory. ASAN reports use-after-poison in HObject.array_part; without ASAN a 50-key proxy for-in under GC pressure segfaults (exit 139).
bugs.latency_signal: Silent memory corruption until heavy GC pressure triggered collection mid-iteration
bugs.credit: found and fixed by claude-opus-5 in Claude Code
bugs.line: listing the keys of a proxy object could segfault
bugs.label: 30 Jul

decisions.title: told the team to rebuild how the engine keeps track of running code
decisions.quote: The VM struct is defined in vm.c3 and we can't import it circularly. Instead, use an opaque pointer pattern: Built-in functions receive `void* vm_opaque` (which is really a VM*)
decisions.summary: The human decided to throw out the first design for tracking what a running program is doing and switch to the way an existing, proven engine does it. It set the shape of everything built afterward.
decisions.impact: Reworked the heart of the engine and gave function calls and nested scopes a foundation that could actually be made correct.
decisions.line: told the team to rebuild the engine core
decisions.label: 22 May

decisions.title: stopped the bug hunt and ordered a clean rebuild of function calls
decisions.quote: the disassembly doesnt matter if youre looking at a wrong implementation1!! just reimplement with the right architecture, forget the current code
decisions.summary: After a string of failed patch attempts, the human said the analysis was pointless because the underlying design was wrong, and told the agent to forget the existing code and rewrite it from the reference engine's design.
decisions.impact: Ended the cycle of incremental fixes and replaced the function-call machinery outright.
decisions.line: stopped the bug hunt and ordered a clean rebuild of function calls
decisions.label: 23 May

decisions.title: asked for a side by side comparison of two rival engines' data layouts
decisions.quote: I need to understand the QuickJS dispatch approach and how Duktape 2.7.0 handles values. Report exact sizes in bytes for each struct and identify the key architectural differences
decisions.summary: The human wanted exact numbers on how much space each engine spends storing a single value, rather than opinions. It gave the project a factual baseline for later design arguments.
decisions.impact: Showed that this engine's values take twice the space of the reference engine's, which limits both speed and how deeply programs can nest calls.
decisions.line: asked for a side by side comparison of two rival engines
decisions.label: 25 May

decisions.title: accepted the deep nesting limit as a design cost and shelved the fix
decisions.quote: The recursion gap is architectural (16-byte TVal vs 8-byte NaN-boxing, no register-binding fast path). Fixing those would require fundamental changes to the value representation and compiler/VM contract — a separate effort.
decisions.summary: The human concluded that the gap in how deeply programs could call themselves came from a basic design choice, not a bug, and deliberately parked the rewrite as its own future project.
decisions.impact: Kept the current round of speed work inside the existing design instead of letting it balloon into a rewrite.
decisions.line: accepted the nesting limit as a design cost
decisions.label: 28 May

decisions.title: asked to pull the engine's giant main loop out into its own routine
decisions.quote: Extract the dispatch loop: The Vm.execute function (starting at line 1085) has a large dispatch loop (lines 1119-4459). Extract lines 1119-4459 into a new function vm_run_dispatch(Vm* vm, uint stop_count).
decisions.summary: One enormous block of code ran every instruction. The human asked for it to be lifted out on its own so it could be started and re-entered from more than one place.
decisions.impact: Made it possible to pause and resume running code, which more advanced language features need.
decisions.line: asked to split the engine's giant main loop
decisions.label: 30 May

decisions.title: gave built-in functions a way to see themselves
decisions.quote: Add `callee_obj` field to BuiltinContext (after `throw_value` field on line 334): callee_obj HObject*; /// The function object being called (for builtins that need to access their own properties).
decisions.summary: The human asked that every built-in function be handed a reference to itself when called, so it could read and update its own attached data.
decisions.impact: Let built-ins such as promise callbacks keep their own state instead of relying on bookkeeping stored elsewhere.
decisions.line: gave built-in functions a way to see themselves
decisions.label: 30 May

decisions.title: split one huge file of built-in functions into many
decisions.quote: We need to split the builtins file into modules I want src/builtins/[name].c3 files. Plan the move carefully to minimize cross dependencies.
decisions.summary: The human asked for the single sprawling file of standard library functions to be broken into one file per area, with the split planned to keep the pieces as independent as possible.
decisions.impact: Let several agents work on different parts of the standard library at once and made the code easier to keep track of.
decisions.line: demanded a root cause for a 70x slow benchmark
decisions.label: 9 Jun

decisions.title: spotted that one code path skipped a safety copy the other one made
decisions.quote: binary_expr copies left to a temp if its a local variable (to avoid clobbering), but the compound assignment path does NOT
decisions.summary: The human noticed that ordinary arithmetic made a scratch copy before working on a variable, but the shorthand version such as x += 1 did not, and pointed at that as the cause of the corruption.
decisions.impact: Pointed the fix directly at making the shorthand version copy, compute, then write back, the same as the normal path.
decisions.line: spotted one code path skipping a safety copy
decisions.label: 11 Jun

decisions.title: refused to accept a cleanup until the deleted code was proven redundant
decisions.quote: did you remove the duplicated definitions? are they defined somewhere else? double check
decisions.summary: An agent removed what it called duplicate definitions. The human pushed back and asked for proof that the same things really existed elsewhere.
decisions.impact: Avoided quietly deleting working functionality and made verification a condition of cleanup work.
decisions.line: refused a cleanup until the deleted code was proven dead
decisions.label: 16 Jun

decisions.title: decided the engine would only support modern JavaScript, not the legacy mode
decisions.quote: this is not duktape, its a new project. I want to support strict only and remove all non-strict features. Write a comprehensive plan for this.
decisions.summary: The human declared this a new project rather than a clone, and asked for a full plan to strip out every trace of JavaScript's older, looser mode.
decisions.impact: Removed a whole category of legacy behavior and made the engine substantially simpler to reason about.
decisions.line: decided to support only modern JavaScript
decisions.label: 20 Jun

decisions.title: ordered a full read-through of the code looking for things to cut
decisions.quote: now lets look at the code. check the advanced c3 skill. read the sources one by one, and find opportunities to simplify and reduce code size. provide a full report.
decisions.summary: The human asked for the sources to be read one by one with a written report on where the code could be simplified and shrunk, rather than waiting for problems to surface.
decisions.impact: Kicked off a quality pass that gave the team specific targets for reducing complexity.
decisions.line: ordered a full read-through hunting for hidden breakage
decisions.label: 30 Jun

decisions.title: asked for a switch to turn off the speed optimizations during testing
decisions.quote: can we add a flag to disable the optimizer? then use that to validate the logic without optimizations, re-enable to adjust the optimizer pass for the new features. add notes on this to the docs
decisions.summary: The human wanted to be able to check that the language logic was right on its own, then turn the optimizations back on and check those separately, with the method written down.
decisions.impact: Separated two kinds of bugs that had been tangled together and made the optimizer independently testable.
decisions.line: asked for a switch to disable optimizations while testing
decisions.label: 6 Jul

decisions.title: traced broken argument unpacking to the wrong technique being used
decisions.quote: Reproduced the bug: function f([a,b]){} called with a generator produces undefined undefined instead of 1 2. Root-caused: the function-param destructuring in functions.c3 uses LDINT index + GETPROP src, index (direct indexed property access) instead of the iterator protocol
decisions.summary: The human reproduced a case where unpacking arguments from a stream of values silently produced nothing, and found that this path grabbed items by position instead of asking the source for them one at a time, unlike the error-handling path that already did it right.
decisions.impact: Identified three places using the wrong technique that needed to be brought in line with the one that worked.
decisions.line: traced broken argument unpacking to the wrong technique
decisions.label: 8 Jul

decisions.title: replaced ad hoc testing with five specific reliability rules
decisions.quote: Make fresh-worker batch the canonical verifier...A contamination detector: run each phase with --workers 1 in a fixed order vs. shuffled order...Guard Heap.reset() against drift
decisions.summary: The human laid out concrete requirements for the test setup, including running each test in a fresh process and adding a checker for tests that only pass because of leftovers from earlier ones.
decisions.impact: Turned chasing intermittent failures into a systematic hunt and made results reproducible.
decisions.line: replaced ad hoc testing with five specific reliability rules
decisions.label: 11 Jul

decisions.title: renamed the tools so the plain one just runs your file
decisions.quote: I think the naming is wrong. I want duktape_c3 to be the normal way to run a file. duktape_c3_debug or something like that to hav the bytecode compiling/inspect
decisions.summary: The human said the naming was backwards and asked that the main command simply run a program, with the inspection tooling moved to a separate, clearly named one.
decisions.impact: Made the everyday command obvious while keeping the debugging tools available.
decisions.line: renamed the tools so the plain one just runs your file
decisions.label: 20 Jul

decisions.title: asked that wrapping a built-in function be allowed
decisions.quote: Fix the Proxy constructor to accept lightfunc (built-in function) values as valid targets.
decisions.summary: The feature for intercepting access to an object rejected the standard built-in functions as targets. The human asked for them to be accepted too.
decisions.impact: Unblocked five conformance tests that wrap built-ins like Math.max.
decisions.line: asked that wrapping a built-in function be allowed
decisions.label: 20 Jul
